claims.text: The intervention is the addition of approximately 0.2–0.4 at.% Al to an Nb–Mo–Ta–W-based refractory high-entropy alloy.
Al is a lightweight alloying element relative to the refractory baseline elements.
Adding 0.2–0.4 at.% Al will induce fine, coherent in situ nanoprecipitates during subsequent heat treatment.
The minor Al addition promotes Al segregation during heat treatment.
Al segregation triggers the formation of the proposed nanoprecipitates.
The nanoprecipitates impede dislocation motion at elevated temperature.
The nanoprecipitates stabilize grain boundaries and impede grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
The Al-modified alloy will have greater high-temperature yield strength than the baseline alloy.
The high-temperature yield-strength improvement will exceed about 100 MPa at temperatures above 1000 °C.
The Al-modified alloy will have better creep resistance than the baseline alloy above 1000 °C.
The Al addition will cause less than approximately a 5% density increase relative to the baseline.
The Al-modified alloy will preserve room-temperature ductility comparable to that of the baseline alloy.
The minor Al addition will strengthen the alloy without forming detrimental brittle intermetallic phases.
The Nb–Mo–Ta–W baseline has acceptable room-temperature properties but limited high-temperature mechanical capability.
Temperatures above 1000 °C are representative of the intended jet-turbine operating conditions.
The beneficial effect depends on forming coherent nanoprecipitates rather than coarse or brittle secondary phases.
The magnitude of strengthening and precipitate morphology will vary with processing conditions.
